asks: Keep Lethbridge-West and Lethbridge-East as in the interim report.

quote: I am writing to express my support for maintaining the current Lethbridge-West and Lethbridge-East constituencies as outlined in the Interim Report.

asks: Keep Heritage Hills in Strathcona-Sherwood Park and do not add Beaumont and parts of Leduc County; add Tofield instead if population is needed.
Commends the interim map for avoiding more hybrids; suggests two more seats each for Calgary and Edmonton and questions the McCauley-Glenora pairing.
Oppose the Okotoks-Diamond Valley option that removes Diamond Valley and adds part of southwest Calgary; keep current or similar boundaries.
Create a southern Alberta district joining portions of Lethbridge with the Crowsnest Pass, Waterton, Cardston, Magrath, Raymond and Stirling.

quote: An electoral district that brings together portions of Lethbridge with the Crowsnest Pass, Waterton Lakes National Park, and the communities of Cardston, Magrath, Raymond and Stirling would meaningfully reflect the realities of life in southern Alberta
note: Asks for one hybrid joining part of Lethbridge to the southwest (Crowsnest and Cardston areas in a single district), which the minority splits between Lethbridge-Fort Macleod-Crowsnest Pass and Lethbridge-Cardston; says nothing of the rest of the city, so not coded L2 direction.

asks: MLA Cyr supports the interim Bonnyville-Cold Lake-St. Paul boundary, asks that the Cold Lake Air Weapons Range stay in it, and asks that Lesser Slave Lake not be eliminated (forwarding a joint northern MLA proposal that restores it).

quote: The loss of yet another northern constituency like Lesser Slave Lake would be extremely difficult for effective representation and would place an unsustainable burden on the remaining northern MLAs.
note: Cyr's own letter; the attached joint northern MLA proposal (pp. 38-46) he 'largely supports' asks to keep Lesser Slave Lake, expanded with the rest of Big Lakes County, Lesser Slave River, Swan Hills and Fort Assiniboine (p. 40: 'A key aspect is maintaining the existence of the Lesser Slave Lake electoral district').
St. Albert named in the joint proposal only as an example of capital-region shared interests supporting hybrids; no request.

asks: Thanks the commission for the new Edmonton seat and for keeping Edmonton ridings within the city; asks to rename Edmonton-South East as Edmonton-Decoteau.
Put west Chestermere in a hybrid riding with adjacent east Calgary neighbourhoods.

quote: An MLA that represents part of Calgary and part of Chestermere would be best positioned to have the right connections in Calgary City Hall
note: Also p. 67: 'including it in a riding that also covers adjacent Calgary neighbourhoods would better reflect how residents live.' Current and interim maps both keep Chestermere apart from Calgary.

asks: Put all of the City of Grande Prairie in one urban riding.
Keep Calgary's added seats, add one more Calgary seat, reconsider the Calgary-Varsity change for University District growth, and keep avoiding urban-rural ridings.
Put all of the City of Grande Prairie in one urban riding.

no request

asks: Keep central Edmonton's riding (do not remove one) so Edmonton gains two seats; thanks the commission for avoiding hybrids.

Do not extend Strathcona-Sherwood Park into Beaumont.
Give Edmonton two added ridings by not consolidating the six central Edmonton ridings; keeps praise for the Mackenzie riding and for limiting hybrids.

quote: As an Indigenous rights lawyer with clients in northeastern Alberta, I commend the EBC’s recommendation to create the riding of Mackenzie.
note: Supports the interim Mackenzie district, which absorbed most of Lesser Slave Lake (K2), as an Indigenous-focused riding; never names Lesser Slave Lake or its dissolution, hence direction and low confidence (rule 5 applied; a narrower reading would leave want blank).

asks: Keep the proposed Calgary-Buffalo and Calgary-Confluence and add a further Calgary seat.
Do not change Strathcona-Sherwood Park: no Beaumont added and Heritage Hills kept.
Supports adding Arbour Lake to Calgary-Edgemont and keeping it urban; asks for more seats in the Legislature.
Reconsider interim splits of urban municipalities (Beaumont, Sherwood Park, Stony Plain/Spruce Grove) and keep each urban municipality within one division where possible.
Revisit the Peace River boundaries, do not remove a northern constituency, and do not group High Level-area First Nations into the predominantly Indigenous Mackenzie riding.

quote: I am deeply concerned about the removal of a constituency in northern Alberta under the proposed map. This decision significantly reduces representation for residents in the north
note: Never names Lesser Slave Lake; the northern seat the interim map removed is Lesser Slave Lake, and she also objects to the proposed Mackenzie riding (pp. 114-115). Coded direction because the district is identified by description only.

asks: Reinstate the sixth central Edmonton riding; keep minimizing hybrids.

MLA Nixon asks for a west-central Eastern Slopes riding with all of Clearwater County, Rocky Mountain House, Sundre, western Mountain View County (plus Cremona), the MD of Bighorn, Stoney and O'Chiese/Sunchild reserves and Banff National Park including the Town of Banff.

quote: I urge the Commission to consider creating a west central Alberta constituency that includes: the entirety of Clearwater County; O’Chiese First Nation 203, Sunchild First Nation 202, and Big Horn 144A; Rocky Mountain House; western Mountain View County
note: Rejection of the interim split, p. 117: 'the decision to divide west central communities like Rocky Mountain House, Sundre, and their surrounding counties into ridings that stretch to the east will not reflect the unique characteristics of these communities'. Also Sundre included.

quote: M.D. of Bighorn; Stoney 142, 143, and 144; and Banff National Park, including the Town of Banff and the Banff Improvement District
note: Wants Bighorn, Stoney reserves and Banff National Park joined to the Rocky Mountain House riding, but including the Town of Banff, which the minority's B1 leaves out; hence B9 (Rocky Mountain House with the Banff townsite), close to B1. Rejects interim Banff-Jasper, p. 118: 'the proposed Banff-Jasper constituency, which relies solely on the Highway 93 corridor [...] is unrealistic to expect a single representative to travel that distance regularly'.

quote: western Mountain View County, using the existing boundary between Rimbey- Rocky Mountain House-Sundre and Olds-Didsbury-Three Hills as the dividing line with the exception of Cremona, which should be included with communities to the west of Highway 22
note: Sundre and western Mountain View County with Rocky Mountain House, west of Highway 22: O1 by the codebook's partial-request rule. Says nothing of Crossfield, Irricana or Beiseker.

asks: Add another Calgary riding; objects to the proposed Calgary-Confluence as lacking common interest.
Keep the existing Lesser Slave Lake district largely intact, adding Swan Hills to meet the population threshold; keep rural boundaries close to current.

quote: This would be a great solution to the population threshold problem in the Lesser Slave Lake ED, and we believe the commission needs to consider this solution to keep the existing Lesser Slave Lake ED largely intact as it is.
note: Solution is adding Swan Hills (about 1,300 people), which both final maps do. No explicit words rejecting the interim dissolution, so rejects left blank.

quote: Thank you for keeping our riding approximately the same. Also thank you for not lumping us with Edmonton.
note: Pinewood (St. Albert) resident in the city-county hybrid; quotes his round 1 letter favouring a grouping of St. Albert east with Morinville, Legal and Bon Accord.

asks: Keep the Highwood constituency and do not merge Okotoks with south Calgary; prefer Okotoks-Diamond Valley.

note: Endorses the interim Mackenzie district (K2), which absorbed most of Lesser Slave Lake; Lesser Slave Lake itself is never named, hence direction.
